title: AI with Godot + blender using gauntlet loop to upscale the graphics.
author: Sinkyz
selftext:
Being inspired by all the cool development with Godot +Blender with Opus and Astra I wanted to create my Vanlife game.   
The game logic is from the kinda games I used to play around 80's and 90's.  
The logic is simple get money to improve your van by doing odd jobs and posting online. Then find a place to sleep before getting too tired and repeat, repeat :)

For me the real improvement was starting to use gauntlet loop to improve the locations and graphics. I think I could have kept pushing but then again it is a fairly simple game and I am happy with the outcome.

comments.body: Looks great! Can you explain what gauntlet loop is?

replies.author: Sinkyz
replies.body: Gauntlet loop simplified is to have two agents one creates the version and second one judges it against a bench mark. I.e. a real car and then you give it a number of rounds. It will get iteratively better as it works. I think there are much better explanations out there but that is it in a nutshell.

replies.author: Double_Suggestion385
replies.body:
A prompt technique that has several agents working in a loop to propose changes, critique them, fix the proposition, implement it,then review and test the implementation.

Takes a lot of tokens but results in a looped incremental improvement with the goal of hitting a given 'standard'.

comments.author: Complex_Original3526
comments.body: Could you elaborate on your workflow more?

replies.author: Sinkyz
replies.body:
Not sure what you mean. Of course, getting to this point there has been a lot of steps and a lot of trial and error. This is the first time I tried to create something a bit bigger so I don't have a great workflow. I used codex, opus 5.5 and some local and open source models for parts of it.

Just as a fun example. I have a van and a lot of this is how I see the #vanlife community from my point of view so when I started I first wanted to think what was "the" element of the gameplay and what I should include and what I should exclude. So I was talking to opus to draft out the game idea and the mechanics. 

Then to get more ideas and to validate it I asked my local model to send the opus created description to 4 different models. I created specific questions both closed and open and then once the answers got back the model ranked, consolidated and build a great way of reviewing them. I got some great feedback from it. Then I created the first playable version started figuring what worked for me and what should be added. Once I had something acceptable I asked my friends to test it and got some more ideas. 

I know this is not the answer you were looking for but hope there is something that helps.
